cards.text: Welcome in, friend! These sayings come from Solomon, copied down by the men of Hezekiah, king of Judah (Proverbs 25:1). First up is a man who gets corrected again and again, and his neck stays stiff as a day-old cookie.

cards.question: Solomon calls this man stiff-necked after much reproof. What happens to a man like that?

answers.text: He is suddenly shattered beyond recovery
He slowly learns his lesson over time
He is given one more chance to listen

cards.text: Now Solomon zooms out to a whole nation: when the righteous flourish, the people rejoice. Then he flips it around.

cards.question: When the wicked rule, the people ___.

cards.text: Next, a man who loves wisdom brings joy to his father. His opposite is the one who keeps company with prostitutes.

cards.question: Solomon says a companion of prostitutes ___ his wealth.

cards.text: Now a king. Solomon says justice is how a king brings stability to the land, steady like a cookie box that doesn't cave in when you stack ten more on top.

cards.question: True or false: Solomon says a man who exacts tribute builds the land up.

cards.text: Then comes the man who flatters his neighbor, the guy going "Love the hat, love the mustache, LOVE the apron!" Friend, that much sugar should make you nervous.

cards.question: What does Solomon say the man who flatters his neighbor is really doing?

answers.text: Spreading a net for his feet
Building a wall around his house
Planting a seed in his field

cards.question: Solomon keeps talking about traps. True or false: he says an evil man is caught by his own sin.

cards.text: And while the evil man's stuck in his own trap, the righteous one sings and rejoices. Then Solomon says the righteous consider the cause of the poor.

cards.question: The righteous consider the cause of the poor. What about the wicked?

answers.text: They have no regard for such concerns
They argue the cause of the poor in court
They give a little and then move on

cards.text: Next, a whole city is heating up, and not the good kind of heat like my ovens. Solomon says mockers are the ones who inflame it.

cards.question: Mockers inflame a city, but the wise turn away ___.

cards.text: Then a wise man goes to court with a fool. Friend, I bet you can already picture how THAT goes.

cards.question: When a wise man goes to court with a fool, how does Solomon say it ends?

answers.text: Raving and laughing with no resolution
The fool finally admits he was wrong
The judge sides quickly with the wise man

cards.text: Back at it, friend! Solomon picks up with men of bloodshed who hate a blameless man.

cards.question: True or false: Solomon says the upright care for the blameless man's life.

cards.text: Now anger, and Solomon says a fool vents all of it. I did that once when my oven timer died mid-batch, and the WHOLE Dorinverse heard about it.

cards.question: A fool vents all his anger. What does a wise man do with his?

cards.text: Next, a ruler with a habit: he listens to lies. Not little ones like me saying I only tasted ONE chocolate chip.

cards.question: True or false: if a ruler listens to lies, Solomon says only a few of his officials will turn wicked.

cards.text: Then Solomon puts two people side by side who couldn't be more different: the poor man and the oppressor.

cards.question: What does Solomon say the poor man and the oppressor have in common?

answers.text: The LORD gives light to the eyes of both
Both of them will stand before the king
Both of them live inside the same city

cards.text: Back to kings, and this one judges the poor with fairness.

cards.question: True or false: Solomon says the throne of the king who judges the poor fairly will last only for his lifetime.

cards.text: Now Solomon says a rod of correction imparts wisdom. Then he looks at a child who gets none of it.

cards.question: A child left to himself disgraces his ___.

cards.text: Then Solomon looks at a season when the wicked thrive. Friend, you can guess that's not the good season.

cards.question: When the wicked thrive, ___ increases.

cards.text: But Solomon says the righteous will see their downfall. Then he says to discipline your son.

cards.question: Solomon says to discipline your son. What will that son give you?

answers.text: Rest and delight to your soul

cards.text: Next, Solomon says where there is no vision, the people cast off restraint. Picture a kitchen with no recipe, flour on the ceiling.

cards.question: In that same line, who does Solomon call blessed?

cards.text: Last stretch, friend! Solomon starts with a servant who can't be corrected by words alone.

cards.question: What's the problem with correcting this servant by words alone?

answers.text: He understands but will not respond
He cannot understand the words at all
He forgets the words by the next morning

cards.text: Then Solomon asks, "Do you see a man who speaks in haste?" Friend, that's me, I once yelled BEST BATCH EVER before I even opened the oven.

cards.question: True or false: Solomon says there is more hope for a fool than for the man who speaks in haste.

cards.text: Next, a servant who has been pampered from his youth. Everything handed to him, every day, for years.

cards.question: A servant pampered from his youth will bring ___ in the end.

cards.text: An angry man stirs up dissension, and a hot-tempered man piles up wrongs. Then Solomon turns to pride.

cards.question: What does Solomon say a man's pride will do to him?
True or false: Solomon says a humble spirit will obtain honor.

cards.text: Then Solomon warns about the partner to a thief, who hates his own soul. He receives the oath, but he does not testify.
Next, Solomon calls the fear of man a snare. Friend, I know that one, I spent years in a junk drawer holding my breath every time a hand reached in.

cards.question: The fear of man is a snare. What does Solomon say about whoever trusts in the LORD?

answers.text: He is set securely on high
He is given a seat by the king

cards.text: Then Solomon says many seek the ruler's favor. Everybody lined up at the palace like it's the last cookie box on the shelf.

cards.question: Many seek the ruler's favor, but a man receives justice from the ___.

cards.text: And Solomon ends the chapter with two people who can't stand each other. He says the unjust man is detestable to the righteous.

cards.question: The unjust man is detestable to the righteous. How do the wicked see the man whose way is upright?

answers.text: He is a friend to them
He is a mystery to them

findings.problem: The question opens with 'Solomon keeps talking about traps.' That lead-in all but says the evil man is caught, which gives away the True answer.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Verse 9 is conditional: 'If a wise man goes to court with a fool.' The card turns it into an event: 'Then a wise man goes to court with a fool.' Card 17 also changes 'If' to 'When'.
Verse 12 is conditional: 'If a ruler listens to lies.' The card states it as fact about a specific ruler: 'a ruler with a habit: he listens to lies.'

The blank asks the baker to guess the exact next word of the line: mother, neighbor or king. Nothing on the earlier cards lets the baker reason out 'mother', so this tests wording the baker hasn't seen.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The question says 'In that same line,' which points back to a story card that is no longer on screen. It needs to say what the line is about, such as where there is no vision.

rule.text: The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: 'Everything handed to him, every day, for years.' Verse 21 says only 'pampered from his youth.' The card adds 'every day' and 'everything,' which stretches the text and adds a time the text doesn't give.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The setup says the two men 'can't stand each other.' That already tells the baker the wicked find the upright man detestable, so it gives away the answer to card 16 and rules out 'a friend' and 'a mystery'.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Stop 1 card 1 cites Proverbs 25:1 to say these sayings are Solomon's, copied by the men of Hezekiah. Every card after that says 'Solomon says.' Proverbs 25:1 introduces 'additional proverbs of Solomon,' but the text never says how far that heading reaches, or that it covers chapter 29.
findings.question: Can Papa Dorin treat the Proverbs 25:1 heading as covering chapter 29 and attribute every saying to Solomon? Or should he leave the speaker open, for example by saying 'the proverb says'?
